{{Quote|In my culture, vocal music is a sacred tradition, and it is the one thing that has kept me alive all this time.|[[Sy Snootles/Legends|Sy Snootles]]|<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" />}}
The '''Pa'lowick''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of sapient amphibians hailing from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Lowick/Legends|Lowick]]. They were divided into two main subspecies, both of which shared the same physical traits suited to their semiaquatic habitat: rotund bodies, slender limbs, eyes that rested on stalks, well-developed lungs, and a proboscis that terminated in a pair of Human-like lips. The major variation between the groups was in the pair of tusks lying under the trunk; these fell out in one species by middle age but remained with the other throughout their lives. Scientists speculated that this was because the tusked variety lived in an area populated by higher densities of predatory life.

A shy and primitive race that held their traditions dear, the Pa'lowick enjoyed offworld contact, eagerly accepting any technology that helped them better accomplish their tasks in the traditional way. Storytelling and song were integral parts of their culture, with songs written for both spirituality and enjoyment. Much of their history was passed down by song; written language arose relatively late in their development. Most members of the species lived as farmers, serving a noble class of royal families.

In the years since their first encounter with [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] miners searching for the [[Pa'Lowick system]]'s legendary [[firegem]]s, the Pa'lowick remained little known away from their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. This changed when [[Larisselle Chatrunis]] was crowned [[Miss Coruscant]] in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] and began a successful singing career. Nevertheless, their world remained isolated, first by an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] blockade, then by a lack of diplomatic interest from the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], however, the invaders paid a visit, destroying Lowick's farming machines in the process. The crops themselves survived the assault, and the planet quickly recovered after the hostilities ceased.

Among the other famous members of the race were [[Sy Snootles/Legends|Sy Snootles]], lead singer of the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band]]; and [[Aneesa Dym]] and [[Neeamesh Dym|her father]], owners of ''[[Dusty Duck]]''.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Who do you think you're fooling? I know who pulled my nose.|[[Keesa]]|<ref name="Tatooine Ghost">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Palowick-AlienEncounters.png|thumb|left|upright|Most Pa'lowick lost their tusks by middle age.]]
Pa'lowick were humanoid amphibians adapted to the peaceful salt marshes of their coastal habitat. Their compact, globular midsections sat atop thin, gangly legs that ended in anisodactylic feet—three toes pointing forward, one back. This configuration allowed them to swiftly navigate still waters, while powerful lungs<ref name="NEGAS" /> in a strong chest helped them swim.<ref name="SWCE">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Their slender arms ended in hands with four digits: three fingers and an opposable thumb.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Pa'lowick sometimes exhibited sharp claws, other times smooth fingertips; in fact, the same individual could display both states at various times.<ref>Sy Snootles has no claws in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] and in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]''. However, in the illustrations for "[[Who's Who in the Max Rebo Band]]" and ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', she is shown with clawed fingers.</ref> Large, well-developed lungs and a buoyant air bladder made Pa'lowick adept swimmers; deflating the air bladder made room for the lungs to overinflate into the abdomen<ref name="NEGAS" /> and permitted them to hold their breath for long periods.<ref>''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' says that Pa'lowick can breathe both air and water. However, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' says that they can merely hold their breath for long spans. The latter source is the more recent and is assumed to supersede ''Ultimate Alien Anthology''.</ref> With their eyes at the end of short stalks, Pa'lowick could hide under water and keep watch for predators. The species had moist, smooth skin with patterns of brown, green, yellow and blue that blended in with their swampy environment.<ref name="NEGAS" /><ref name="X-Wing Rogue Squadron ½">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron ½|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' ½]]</ref><ref name="Spy Girls">{{CWACite|7|Spy Girls}}</ref> Skin markings varied by individual; male Pa'lowick sported angular shapes, while females showed more rounded mottling.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Due to their amphibious nature, Pa'lowick were most comfortable in moist conditions; arid environments harmed their skin, nose, and throat.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" /><ref name="ATBPO">"[[And the Band Played On: The Band's Tale]]," ''[[Tales from Jabba's Palace]]''</ref> They were also particularly susceptible to air pollution.<ref name="Hnn-Study: Pollution Standards Still Endanger Many">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49|life/13328_4.html|Study: Pollution Standards Still Endanger Many}}</ref> Over a few weeks, however, a Pa'lowick could adjust to such conditions.<ref name="ATBPO" />

The most prominent feature of the Pa'lowick physiology was a 30-centimeter,<ref name="CSWE III">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', Vol. III</ref> prehensile,<ref name="ATBPO" /> expressive,<ref name="SWCE" /> tubular snout that ended in pair of [[Human/Legends|Human]]-like lips.<ref name="NEGAS" /> In younger Pa'lowick, two sharp,<ref name="UAA" /> retractable,<ref name="SWCE" /> upward-pointing tusks—handy weapons should the Pa'lowick be attacked—protruded from a second mouth at the base of this mouth-stalk.<ref name="UAA" /> The second mouth was larger and wider than the one at the end of the snout and allowed growing, energy-hungry Pa'lowick to eat more food. As a Pa'lowick entered maturity, the need for this extra nutrition subsided; in most members of the species, the tusks fell out, and flesh overgrew the second mouth, causing it to completely disappear and be reabsorbed by middle age. However, in one group, the second mouth and tusks persisted throughout the Pa'lowick's life. Scientists speculated that this subspecies was the older of the two, but genetic experiments proved inconclusive. There was certainly evolutionary pressure on these Pa'lowick to keep their tusks, as they lived in an area with a greater concentration of dangerous fauna.<ref name="NEGAS" />

[[File:Snootles_with_claws.png|thumb|right|upright|Pa'lowick sometimes exhibited sharp claws.]]
Although the average Pa'lowick stood 1.6 meters tall,<ref name="NEGAS" /> a height at which 48 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] was normal.<ref name="HTHTT" /> The species exhibited a great range of heights; some members were as short as 0.9 meters while others grew as tall as 1.8 meters.<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> They tended toward the upper end of that range, with the average height at 1.6 meters.<ref name="UAA" /> Their air bladders made them surprisingly lightweight for their size.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Pa'lowick were oviparous, and females tended to their eggs until they hatched.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Pa'lowick entered puberty at age 12. Adulthood began at age 17, and middle age at 45. Life expectancy for the species was 75 years.<ref name="UAA" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|I haven't heard anything like this since I attended a benefit for a tone-deaf Pa'lowick—and boy, those guys could wail.|[[Droma]]|<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic III: Reunion">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic III: Reunion]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Palowick-EGAS.png|thumb|left|upright|Singing was both an entertaining pastime and a sacred rite for Pa'lowick.]]
The Pa'lowick lived in numerous large, independent communities spread throughout the equatorial regions of their homeworld, [[Lowick/Legends|Lowick]], sheltered by roofed, nestlike homes of grass, mud, and reeds. These groups followed a feudal system of government, with a complex but adaptive system of nobility determining the ruling families.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Most Pa'lowick toiled as peasant farmers, while others served as fishers, hunters, and storytellers.<ref name="UAA" /> They were natural scavengers, and most Pa'lowick supplemented their lifestyle by hunting and gathering.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The long Pa'lowick snout and the tongue inside were perfectly adapted to piercing giant [[marlello]] duck eggs and slurping down the yolk,<ref name="CSWE III" /> a Pa'lowick favorite.<ref name="NEGAS" /> [[Veeji fruit]] was another popular food; it grew abundantly in the rain forest year round.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Other Pa'lowick food sources were fish, reptiles, and water birds found in their marshy habitat.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Children were raised and educated by the community.<ref name="NEGAS" />

To the Pa'lowick, songs and stories were not only the height of entertainment, they were sacred aspects of the species' heritage. Pa'lowick music ran the gamut of genres and subjects, although religious music was particularly common. Cultural heritage, such as history, genealogy, and parables, was largely passed down orally. Every Pa'lowick community had a dedicated storyteller; the esteem afforded this individual made the position a coveted one.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Large lungs made the Pa'lowick hearty singers<ref name="NEGAS" /> and afforded at least some members of the species the ability to scream loudly and disarm opponents in combat.<ref name="HTHTT" />

Although those Pa'lowick who kept their tusks through life were overall more aggressive,<ref name="NEGAS" /> the Pa'lowick were shy and patient creatures of ritual and habit<ref name="NEGAS" /> who stood by their traditions and customs in the face of outside contact.<ref name="UAA" /> Nevertheless, they were not completely hidebound; Pa'lowick were friendly to outsiders and fascinated by the advanced technology they brought. The beings eagerly adopted those items that increased their productivity—provided such devices did not disrupt their traditions.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Nevertheless, their world had little to offer [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large, so offworld contact was rare.<ref name="UAA" /> Their overall level of technology remained largely feudal in nature with only a few choice bits of higher tech in general use. With the Pa'lowick [[Larisselle Chatrunis]]'s win of the [[Miss Coruscant]] pageant in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] and her subsequent singing career, recorded Pa'lowick music came into demand across the galaxy and on the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]]. Foodstuffs (especially the popular veeji fruit), primitive crafts, and recorded music were Lowick's major exports.<ref name="NEGAS" />

The native language of the Pa'lowick was called [[Lowickese]]. When the species first came into contact with offworlders, the tongue had no written form. Pa'lowick scholars adopted the [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] [[Writing/Legends|alphabet]], and over the years, most Pa'lowick became literate in Lowickese. Written Lowickese looked like pure nonsense to outsiders. The Pa'lowick vocal apparatus allowed them to speak Basic with ease.<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
[[File:Larisselle_Chatrunis.jpg|thumb|right|[[Larisselle Chatrunis]] brought the Pa'lowick to galactic attention when she won the [[Miss Coruscant]] pageant in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. Her powerful performance during the competition made Pa'lowick singers renowned galaxy-wide.]]
The Pa'lowick hailed from the planet Lowick, in the [[Pa'Lowick system]], part of the [[Calaron sector/Legends|Calaron sector]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].<ref name="Gundark">''[[Gundark's Fantastic Technology: Personal Gear]]''</ref> The planet was made up of vast seas and rugged, mountainous land masses. In the equatorial climes, mountains gave way to the humid swamps and vibrant, green rain forests in which the Pa'lowick evolved.<ref name="NEGAS" /> Over time, the species spread throughout the equatorial region and splintered into independent communities. A complex system of nobility developed, and the species advanced to a feudal level of technology with peasant agriculture as the backbone of the social order.<ref name="NEGAS" />

Sometime between [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]] and [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], spacefaring miners became the first outsiders to visit Lowick.<ref>This date is inconsistent from source to source. ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', dates this discovery to before the Clone Wars but then contradicts itself with a date of [[10 BBY/Legends|10 BBY]]. Earlier sources, on the other hand, place it in [[6 BBY/Legends|6 BBY]], well into the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial era]]. The former is the most recent source and is assumed to supersede previous publications. Furthermore, the biography of [[Aneesa Dym]] in the [http://www.starwars.com/databank/starship/dustyduck/index.html Databank] places her on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in 32 BBY, which suggests an earlier date of contact. Finally, ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places Lowick's discovery sometime between 1,000 BBY and 25 BBY.</ref> In the system's [[Lowick asteroid belt|asteroid belt]], the miners found a type of gemstone whose volatility caused it to explode when exposed to various types of radiation. The discovery had obvious applications in demolitions and mining, and a steady flow of prospectors was soon making regular stops in the system to gather what became known as [[Lowickan Firegem|Lowickan firegems]]. Traders arrived as well, selling the Pa'lowick advanced galactic technology in exchange for foodstuffs. Despite their natural conservatism, Pa'lowick communities traded for advanced items that seemed useful but did not pose a threat to their traditional way of life, such as automated harvesting machinery.<ref name="AE" /> Meanwhile, [[Larisselle Chatrunis]] won the [[Miss Coruscant]] pageant in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] and embarked on a successful singing career, bringing the Pa'lowick to the galactic eye and ear.<ref name="NEGAS" /> By the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Lowick had been swallowed up into the expanding borders of [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

After the fall of the Old Republic, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was eager to monopolize extraction of firegems and established a blockade of the Pa'Lowick system,<ref name="AE" /> which by this point was once again independent of Hutt Space.<ref name="Atlas" /> The Empire deemed Lowick itself to be mostly useless, and the Pa'lowick were spared the horrors of enslavement and forced labor.<ref name="UAA" /> Upon the conclusion of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], a few Pa'lowick nobles flirted with joining the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], but innate disinterest in politics and a lack of any diplomatic overtures from the galactic government stopped their plans from coming to fruition. After years of relative peace, Lowick was invaded by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. The aggressors destroyed the automated harvesting machines used by Pa'lowick farmers, but they left the crops themselves unmolested. When the hostilities drew to an end, the Pa'lowick were thus relatively hale and hearty and able to quickly recover their place in the galactic economy.<ref name="NEGAS" /> The [[Shi'ido]] [[Sentientologist|anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] included an entry on the Pa'lowick in his publication ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', which he published at some point during the rule of New Republic.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" /> By [[137 ABY]], Lowick had become a [[Hutt Dependency]].<ref name="Atlas" />

==Pa'lowick in the galaxy==
{{Quote|I think separation is very, like, traumatic. When it happens to families, it's sad. But when it happens to an entire galaxy, which has millions of families, it's even sadder.|Larisselle Chatrunis on the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]]|<ref name="Hnn">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|52|life/13418_1.html|Chatrunis Crowned Miss Coruscant}}</ref>}}
[[File:Sam_Snootles.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Some Pa'lowick, such as [[Sam Snootles]], managed to find a niche off their homeworld.]]
Most Pa'lowick were content to remain on Lowick, set up a "nest," and leave the rest of the galaxy to mind its own affairs.<ref name="UAA" /> Still, some made it off their homeworld,<ref name="AE" /> often lured by wondrous tales told by strangers from distant worlds.<ref name="UAA" /> With nothing but a primitive, slow-paced life behind them, such Pa'lowick often proved naïve wanderers and easy marks; after only a little time abroad, they could easily find themselves creditless and forced to take up less-than-savory vocations to survive. It was not uncommon to find Pa'lowick living as beggars, criminals, or even slaves. Still, some members of the species managed to establish a niche as [[Fringer/Legends|fringers]], [[Scout/Legends|scouts]],<ref name="UAA" /> and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]]. As early as [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the Pa'lowick [[Aneesa Dym]] and [[Neeamesh Dym|her father]] had made a name for themselves as smugglers on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]] in their ship the ''[[Dusty Duck]]'',<ref name="Dusty Duck">{{DB|starship|dustyduck|Dusty Duck}}</ref> [[Sam Snootles]] lived and worked on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] as early as [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="Clone Wars Chapter 21">{{CW|21}}</ref> and the proboscis-like [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocoder]] of the [[SP-4 analysis droid/Legends|SP-4 analysis droid]] suggested that a Pa'lowick had a hand it its design.<ref name="DB-SP-4">{{DB|droid|sp4|SP-4}}</ref>

Other Pa'lowick left their homeworld to pursue a career in show business. Since Lowick's introduction to the wider galaxy, Pa'lowick singers traveled the galaxy, performing in cantinas far and wide, both solo and as part of ensembles. Advanced recording technology expanded their fanbase, making these singers some of the most popular performers on the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]]. Galactic music critics were among their most vocal supporters. Two famous Pa'lowick singers, rumored to be rivals, were [[Larisselle Chatrunis]] and [[Sy Snootles/Legends|Sy Snootles]].<ref name="NEGAS" /> Chatrunis leapt into the public eye when she used her powerful singing voice to win the [[Miss Coruscant]] pageant in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]. She spun her win into a lucrative musical career, only to have it cut short by Emperor [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] anti-alien policies. The performer later joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], using her performances and supposed rivalry with Snootles as a front for her outlawed activities.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">{{CSWECite|I|120|Chatrunis}}</ref> Sy Snootles was the lead singer of the [[Max Rebo Band/Legends|Max Rebo Band]] until that group broke up in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. She tried to make her way as a solo artist, but her records sold dismally<ref name="Snootles DB">{{DB|character|sysnootles|Snootles, Sy}}</ref> when most listeners found her singing voice too bizarre to enjoy.<ref name="SWCE" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Kiss me. Kiss me.|Industrial Light and Magic crew member playing with the Sy Snootles puppet|<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Sy_Snootles_with_puppeteers.jpg|thumb|right|upright|The Pa'lowick used for the 1983 release of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] was an articulated puppet.]]
The character Sy Snootles introduced the as-yet-unnamed Pa'lowick to ''Star Wars'' continuity in the Jabba's-palace sequences of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] (1983). After the puppet (dubbed "Ms. Snooty" during production) had already been designed, the producers decided to make the character the lead singer of the Max Rebo Band. [[Phil Tippett]] revisited the creature to add articulation to the snout and enable it to "sing," and [[George Lucas]] suggested that she be given large, red, "Mick Jagger lips."<ref name="Snootles DB" /> The puppet was 147 cm tall and had a 30 cm snout. It required two operators: one who performed the legs from beneath a raised stage, and another who moved the arms and microphone from above. In closeups, a separate puppet with no legs was used.<ref name="BTM" /> When Lucas revamped the main song-and-dance number performed by the Max Rebo Band for the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] release of ''Jedi'' (1997), the Pa'lowick was redesigned as a computer-generated character and lost her tusks and second mouth.<ref name="Snootles DB" />

[[File:Anatomy_of_Myself.png|thumb|left|"Anatomy of Myself" feature from ''Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas'']]
[[West End Games]]' roleplaying supplement ''[[Alien Encounters]]'' was the first look at the Pa'lowick as a species. Both the [[West End Games]] and [[Wizards of the Coast]] ''Star Wars'' roleplaying games provide rules for players to portray Pa'lowick characters. In West End's version, they are more perceptive than other species but slightly slower.<ref name="AE" /> In Wizards' game, Pa'lowick are weaker than most species but nimbler and more perceptive.<ref name="UAA" /> The book [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']] created the concept of Pa'lowick being born with two mouths and tusks which disappear with age, thus reconciling both the original and ''Special Edition'' versions of the species.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Alien Species" />

The [[1993]] reference book ''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]'' showed Pa'lowick to have head plumage, "percussive toes," a "kaleidoscopic snout," a "multi-grottoed mouth" and upper limbs that doubled as ears.<ref name="MAGL">''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]''</ref> However, [[Lucasfilm]] employee [[Leland Chee]], who maintains the [[Holocron continuity database]], has indicated that information contained in the book is [[Canon|non-canonical]] unless reused in another source.<ref name="Chee">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=152583&start=690#14724917|thread=Holocron continuity database questions|user=[[Leland Chee|Leland Y Chee]]|date=2006-05-03|time=5:45 PM|quote=And is information from Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas canon? Unless referred to by a source that is in-continuity, the information is non-continuity.}}</ref>
